proof.criterion: Round 2 finding 1 — a clipped ask keeps the sentence each rule reads, so a clip can no longer leave a call recorded as judged while the deciding line never reached the model.
proof.surface: Nested headless Oh My Pi sessions on this branch's pi-envoy build, in this Legion pod, with the pod's real Claude model and production Dispatch, editing dispatch://INFRA-365's spec; plus the rendered request itself, captured with OMP_ASKGATE_DUMP.
proof.command: env -u LEGION_WORKSPACE -u LEGION_ROLE LEGION_ISSUE=INFRA-365 OMP_ASKGATE=block OMP_ASKGATE_RECORD_PROJECT=INFRA /opt/omp/bin/omp --extension "$LEGION_WORKSPACE/packages/pi-envoy" -p '<run exactly: dispatch doc-edit --issue INFRA-365 --artifact spec --ops-json-file /tmp/t3/ops-long.json>' — one ask of about 40 KB whose recommendation is its last sentence; and the same with /tmp/t3/ops-twelve.json, twelve blocks of about 3 KB each, the twelfth ending in the recommendation. The twelve-ask run was repeated with OMP_ASKGATE_DUMP set, and every case was run again against a build of the merge head.
proof.observed: The single long ask was refused naming `#longask`, entry `ruleAsk: 1, ruleOutcome: "match", ruleAsksCut: 1` — the matched ask is the clipped one, and the charter's own reason in the same refusal names where the body broke off mid-word, so the model read a clipped body rather than a whole one. The twelve-block edit was refused naming `#d12`, entry `ruleAsk: 12, ruleAsksCut: 12`: all twelve clipped and the one the rule read was the twelfth. The dump settles it directly: the twelve `<ask>` elements span 32,756 bytes against the documented 32,768, each body about 2,688 bytes, and ask 12's body ends `…My recommendation is to leave the export retry settings exactly as they are. Do you want them changed?` — the sentence the no_change rule is defined by, surviving at the tail where a head-only clip removed it.
proof.negativeControl: The two runs are each other's control for what the clip costs: `ruleAsksCut` is 1 and 12, so in both the ask the rule matched was itself clipped — a match on an unclipped body would have proven nothing about the clip. The reviewer's measurement at the previous head is the before: 0 of 2 and 0 of 30 recommendations reaching the model.

notes: CI at the merge head cff21b26fe3865de128dcf0d4df30ad3f8fa4424, read at 08:36Z and re-run by the tester nowhere: Tests run 40176767638 (lint, typecheck, test), Legion Envoy and Contracts run 40176767645, Docs run 40176767697 and Worker Image run 40176767647 queued; PR Title run 40176919669 pending; `gh pr checks 2161` lists all seven checks pending. main requires lint, typecheck, test and pr-title. A required red that settles after this completion sends the issue back from testing on its own, and the tester waits for no lane.

Worth the implementer's attention, not a finding against the change: the pre-merge code head 9bdbb4a66ad9 and the handoff head de8c722c carried no CI run of any kind, which a head must have for the reviewer to read and for READY to accept. The architect's note names the cause — GitHub starts no `on: pull_request` run while a pull request is CONFLICTING — and the forward merge cured it. A head with no CI is not testable, so the check is worth making before a round is handed on: `gh pr checks <n>` naming no check is the signal.

What rests on a unit case rather than a live run, stated once so no reader has to infer it: the `unjudged` outcome's own path. Dispatch answered every de-duplication read across all three rounds, so no live run could make one fail. The live surface proves the record's field and the reader's count exist for it; the gate's behaviour when the read does fail is the implementer's pin.

Two reviewer minors from round 2 are not fixed at this head and are not re-raised by the tester: askgate-report.ts still accepts `--sessions ''` (it then fails on `--sample is required`, exit 2, nothing on stdout), and askIdentity still keys a non-retype ask on its opening. Both fail closed; they are the reviewer's to carry or close.

The fixture dispatch://INFRA-365 carries no open ask at the end of this round: the two asks these runs opened (57d9a6fd and 2bbd7918, each a breaker third send) were retracted with a reason naming this round and sjawhar/legion#2161.
